verdicts.argument: I checked the materiality skeptic's pages. The warning was not deleted. ABBV:10k_FY2025.md p.13 still says 'The effect of reducing prices and reimbursement could significantly impact revenues for certain of our products', and p.18 still says the IRA 'could significantly impact AbbVie's results of operations'. Both sentences are identical on ABBV:10k_FY2024.md p.13 and p.18. Only the MD&A repeat (FY2024 p.36) is gone, and that half of the candidate collapses. What remains is the new 340B-share sentence (FY2025 p.23) and the MFN/direct-to-patient spillover sentence (p.19). These are still not said on any call, but the filing gives no dollar size, and the MFN half restates a press-released deal. Unsaid but unsized risk wording does not make a finding.
verdicts.correction: Not a standalone finding. At most, use the p.23 340B-share sentence, with the 2026-10-02 340B rebate-pilot release, as context in the product or gross-to-net discussion.

round2.conceded: The 'deleted would-significantly-impact sentence' was the novel half of the candidate, and it is wrong: the sentence survives in Item 1 on p.13 and p.18 of both years. Without it, and without any derivable dollar figure, the candidate fails materiality.
round2.held: The 340B-share admission (FY2025 p.23) is still new and still absent from every call and release I searched. That is obviousness context, not grounds to keep the finding.
round2.narrowed: Changed from held (minor) to refuted (major). Demoted from a finding to supporting context.

verdicts.argument: Verified on ABBV:10k_FY2025.md p.49. Managed Care rebate provisions fell from 24,127 to 22,307 in the column next to the Medicaid and Medicare jump (15,866 to 21,283). Total rebates and chargebacks went from $59.3B to $65.1B. The implied deduction ratio moves from about 51.3% to 51.6%, roughly 0.3 points. This is a channel shift under Part D redesign, which management guided on the 2024Q4 call as about $2B net.
verdicts.correction: Drop it. The only forward angle is whether the January 2026 'low prices in Medicaid' commitment lifts the total ratio in the FY2026 10-K, which cannot be observed yet.

round2.conceded: In round 1 I left open a possible residual of about $3B beyond the guided Part D effect. The managed-care offset on the same page closes it, so there is no residual left to rescue.
round2.held: The obviousness kill stands independently: the Part D redesign effect was guided in dollars and product by product, and gross-to-net was asked in 8 of 10 quarters.
round2.narrowed: Severity raised from major to fatal, and the round-1 residual correction is withdrawn.

verdicts.argument: Verified on ABBV:companies/ABBV/10q_2025Q2.md p.5: at June 30, 2025, accounts receivable were 12,637 and inventories 4,960. Both are above the December 31, 2025 levels of 12,589 and 4,951. There was no Q4 build. The 15% rise comes from a low December 2024 base, and nothing unwound afterwards: receivables were 13,824 at June 2026.

round2.conceded: In full. I held c03 on the grounds that nobody had sized it, but there is nothing to size. The 'slight inventory destock' remark on the 2026Q1 call that I cited is a routine quarterly comment, not evidence of an unwind.

verdicts.argument: Obviousness is unchanged. Eye Care disappeared from the Q1 2026 earnings release table (ABBV:earnings/2026-04-29_abbv-20260331xexhibit991.md p.6) and from both 2026 10-Qs without a note, and no 2025Q4 to 2026Q2 call mentions it. On materiality I accept the other skeptic's points. The restated bucket was already falling about 9.7% before the change. The TrumpRx-exposed Alphagan/Combigan U.S. line was only $53M. The fold has no P&L effect.
verdicts.correction: Keep it only as a low-weight 'segment and product table changes' row: AbbVie silently folded $2.1B (3.4% of revenue) of a declining franchise into 'All other', and the restatement reconciles exactly. Drop the TrumpRx motive, because the $53M Alphagan/Combigan line cannot carry it. This is a transparency observation, not an earnings hit.

round2.conceded: The -10% decline is not new, and the TrumpRx link is trivial in dollars.
round2.held: It is unsaid and fits a category the case names explicitly ('products quietly no longer broken out'). It is good enough for one row of a five-finding table, but not as the sharpest needle.
round2.narrowed: The claim is now about disclosure only, with no motive and no hidden decline.

verdicts.argument: Verified on ABBV:10q_2026Q2.md p.15. The weighted-average probability is 93% within a 38%-100% range, weighted by relative fair value, against 100% at December 2025. The projected payment years run 2026-2044, but the weighted average stays at 2030. Their arithmetic is right: the combination share is (100-93)/(100-38), about 11%, or about $3B of the $27.5B. Is it unsaid? Yes. Searches of every transcript, earnings release and 8-K for '2044', 'contingent' or royalty-on-combinations find nothing. The tail first appears in the June 2026 10-Q; the 2026Q1 10-Q (p.14) still showed 2026-2037 at 100%. Is it material? The $3B present value is about 4.9% of 2025 revenue and about $1.70 a share pre-tax (3,000/1,773). It runs through GAAP fair-value charges, and p.33 names 'favorable clinical trial results for pipeline assets in combination with Skyrizi' as a driver of the H1 2026 charge. Adjusted EPS excludes it. The more material point is economic rather than accounting: a royalty of roughly 16-18% of sales now attaches to the combination products that management sells as the next immunology leg ('combination approaches with SKYRIZI or RINVOQ as a backbone', 2025Q3, grade B, Robert A. Michael). That margin drag reaches 2044 and grows only if the combinations succeed.
verdicts.correction: Use it as the sharpest needle, sized honestly. Since June 2026, AbbVie's Skyrizi partner royalty also covers Skyrizi-combination pipeline assets through 2044. That tail is about $3B (11%) of the $27.5B liability at a 38% probability of approval. It is about $1.70 a share of GAAP-only charges now, and a royalty of roughly 16-18% on any successful combination later. No call or release has mentioned it. Do not claim it raised the charge run-rate (H1 2026 3,905 is below H1 2025 4,313), and do not present $27.5B as an annual cost.

round2.conceded: The tail is about $3B of present value, not the whole $27.5B. The weighted-average payment year is unchanged at 2030, and the fair-value charge run-rate did not rise. The annual royalty cash was already disclosed on calls.
round2.held: It is both unsaid and material enough. A $3B present value is about 5% of revenue and about $1.70 a share of GAAP charges. Strategically, it puts a royalty on the combination franchise management calls 'underappreciated'. It is the only ABBV candidate that passes both lenses.
round2.narrowed: The claim is now limited to the June 2026 combination tail at about $3B. The 2037 extension, the $27.5B headline and any 'grew the drag' language are all dropped.

verdicts.argument: The other skeptic's Part D bound, verified on the CMS IPAY2027 fact sheet p.2, puts Vraylar's 2024 Part D gross at $1,137M against $3,260M of U.S. net revenue. Linzess's Part D gross already exceeds AbbVie's U.S. net. Combined 2027 exposure is under about $0.8B, which is consistent with the CEO's on-record 'will not impact our long-term guidance'.
verdicts.correction: Drop it. The corrected exposure (about 1.3% of revenue) is what management has already signalled.

round2.conceded: Their materiality bound is better than my round-1 framing. It shows the 'deflection' was accurate, not evasive, which removes the remaining non-obvious angle.
round2.held: The obviousness kill: the CMS cuts are headlines, the Imbruvica IRA effect is in prepared remarks, and two analysts asked about Vraylar and Linzess on the record.
round2.narrowed: No change in verdict. The 'what would make it non-obvious' route (Part D share data) has now been tested and points to a small exposure.

verdicts.argument: The other skeptic says the Crohn's-only status rests on grade C/D calls. It does not: the official Q1 2026 earnings release (ABBV:earnings/2026-04-29_abbv-20260331xexhibit991.md p.3) announces a subcutaneous induction filing only for Crohn's disease. Their revenue check (Skyrizi U.S. +26.3% in H1 2026 during the Tremfya SC rollout) adds a materiality failure to the obviousness one.
verdicts.correction: Drop it. The label contrast belongs in the product slot only.

round2.conceded: No visible revenue effect, and the sensitivity is below the 1% threshold.
round2.held: Fatal on obviousness. The Crohn's-only filing is verifiable from an A-grade company document (the earnings release), not just from grade C/D calls.

verdicts.argument: The other skeptic held this at minor, but their own corrections deepen the obviousness problem. In dollars, J&J's exposure per point of U.S. price is larger ($53.8B U.S. revenue against AbbVie's $46.6B). J&J's pledge is larger per year (about $13.8B against $10B). Management had already stated the capex part on the grade-B 2025Q3 call ('at least $10 billion of capital in The US over the next ten years'). What remains is AbbVie's highest U.S. share of revenue, 76.2%, which an analyst put to the CEO on that call and which sits in every 10-K geography table.
verdicts.correction: Use it as company-selection context in the deck (why AbbVie is the most U.S.-weighted MFN signatory), not as a finding.

round2.conceded: The numbers are correct, and the CEO did answer Breen's question in substance, so the reader's word 'declined' should go.
round2.held: Refuted on obviousness. A ratio stated on a call plus a press-released pledge is not a needle. Once corrected, the 'most exposed' and 'record pledge' claims are true only on narrow bases.
round2.narrowed: Recast as context for the company-choice slide.

verdicts.argument: I agree with the other skeptic that Skyrizi is the right pick on size (28.7% of revenue) and that the NADAC-versus-ASP support compares different dosage forms and channels. I still hold that the stated edge, IV versus subcutaneous induction, is public.
verdicts.correction: Keep Skyrizi as the product. Lead the fine print with the label hepatotoxicity contrast (drug:skyrizi:label_sections.md p.19 against Tremfya's above-label case), with IV-only UC induction as a secondary point. Tie it to c05, the royalty on Skyrizi combinations, as the financial link. Restate NADAC and ASP as two separate price series.

round2.conceded: The product choice itself stands, and the NADAC/ASP correction is right.
round2.held: The induction edge is not fine print the market missed.
round2.narrowed: Severity lowered from major to minor. Only the edge needs reframing, not the pick.

overall: After round 2, AbbVie has one candidate that is both unsaid and material: the June 2026 Skyrizi-combination royalty tail (c05). It is about $3B of present value, about $1.70 a share of GAAP-only charges, and a royalty of roughly 16-18% on the combination strategy management promotes. Eye Care (c04) survives only as a low-weight disclosure row. Everything else is either already said (c02, c06, c07, c08) or numerically wrong (c01's 'deleted' sentence, c03's build), so AbbVie cannot fill five strong rows from this set without new digging.
